newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's government slims gap in popularity poll.
newsitem.headline: Spain's government slims gap in popularity poll.

text.p: Spain's government improved its standing in a key popularity poll on Sunday but still remained 3.2 points behind the main opposition Socialist Workers Party.

In the quarterly survey published by the daily El Pais, 25.3 percent of those polled said they would vote for the Socialists (PSOE) at the next election, while 22.1 percent would vote for the ruling Popular Party (PP).
In the previous poll conducted in October, the PSOE led by 4.6 points, with 27.8 percent saying they would vote for the Socialists.
The winter survey showed that 51 percent thought the government had not fulfilled its election promises compared with 59 percent in the previous poll.
The survey of 1,200 adults conducted between January 11 and 15 also found that 32 percent approved of the government's performance so far, compared with 30 percent who disapproved.

Fifty percent said they did not support the pact between the government and its nationalist allies which they feel weakens and conditions the government's actions. Some 57 percent said the influence of the nationalist parties on the government was excessive.
The PP formed a pact with the nationalist parties after it fell short of an absolute majority at the general election in March last year.
Former Prime Minister Felipe Gonzalez once again scooped poll position as the favourite leader, scoring 5.3 out of 10 compared with 5.0 for the current prime minister, Jose Maria Aznar.
The survey by polling agency Demoscopia has a margin of error of 2.9 percent.
